gloss: haphazard; unplanned; playing it by ear

definitions.gloss: haphazard; unplanned; playing it by ear; random; improvised
definitions.explanation: Acting without a plan or preparation, just dealing with things as they come. Can describe either a carefree attitude or reckless disorganization.

examples.japanese: {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧だ。
⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}て→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ず、{行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{行動|こうどう}→行動：02728_koudou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I acted without making a plan, just playing it by ear.

examples.japanese: {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{経営|けいえい}→経営：02740_keiei⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦いずれ→いずれ：01789_izure⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Haphazard management will eventually lead to failure.

notes:
Can carry either a positive or negative nuance depending on context. When describing travel or leisure, it suggests a carefree, adventurous spirit. In work or business contexts, it implies irresponsible lack of planning. Functions as a noun modified by ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧, or as an adverbial modifier with ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧.

ETYMOLOGY:
From {行|い}き{当|あ}たる (to come across by chance) + ⟦ばったり→ばったり：03701_battari⟧ (suddenly encountering). The doubling creates an emphatic sense of doing whatever one happens upon.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{旅|たび}→旅：03407_tabi⟧: an unplanned trip
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧: an aimless lifestyle
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{決|き}める→決める：00858_kimeru⟧: to decide on the fly
- {行|い}き{当|あ}たりばったり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行動|こうどう}→行動：02728_koudou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to act haphazardly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧とこ⟦{勝負|しょうぶ}→勝負：01437_shoubu⟧: playing it by ear; taking one's chances — similar meaning but focuses more on the element of risk
- ⟦{無計画|むけいかく}→無計画：27016_mukeikaku⟧: unplanned; without a plan — a more neutral, descriptive term
- {場当|ばあ}たり: ad hoc; improvised — often negative, implying stopgap measures without thinking ahead
